overview: The Almoravids governed from Marrakesh and connected Saharan routes with North African and Iberian towns. Their rule supported major religious buildings and crafts, while their capital helped shape the urban geography of the western Islamic world.

items.text: Marrakesh was an Almoravid foundation. Its palm grove is traditionally attributed to their period, linking the capital with a managed cultivated landscape.
Ali ibn Yusuf commissioned a richly worked mosque minbar in 1137. It later became associated with the Kutubiyya Mosque.
Textile manufacture in Almeria shows that Almoravid cultural production included luxurious fabrics as well as mosque building.
Almoravid power connected important ports with trans-Saharan commerce. The state's economy crossed both sea and desert.
The Almohads replaced Almoravid rule in Marrakesh in the mid-twelfth century and retained the city as a capital.
